observation_summary: The application throws an OutOfMemoryError when processing a large number of data points because it attempts to allocate a full n x n matrix for weights, even when the weight matrix is diagonal.
reasoning_summary: The root cause is an inefficient algorithmic choice in the Weight class constructor. It uses MatrixUtils.createRealMatrix(dim, dim) to create a full matrix for what is essentially a diagonal weight set. This is a procedural/computational strategy error where the implementation fails to account for the memory complexity of large datasets, requiring a change in the algorithm used to represent the weight matrix (e.g., using a diagonal matrix representation instead of a full one).
evidence_used: Bug report description: 'an nxn full matrix is created (and copied) when a n elements vector is used. This exhausts memory when n is large.'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix might involve a new class (e.g., DiagonalMatrix), the root cause is the current implementation's choice to use a full matrix algorithm for a diagonal data structure, which is a procedural/algorithmic inefficiency.
The issue is not an incorrect constant or variable initialization, but the fundamental choice of data structure and allocation strategy for the weight matrix.
